interpretation: The Damodarpur series records administration in Puṇḍravardhana-bhukti. It establishes Gupta provincial evidence, not the date when all of Ratnapīṭha was taken from Kamarupa.
limitations: The dated documents do not prove identical Ratnapīṭha boundaries or a continuous transfer narrative.
ownership_interval_established: No; this is an evidence window, not continuous ownership
sources: Gupta-era north Bengal records; Damodarpur charters, c.443/44–543/44; edition references collected in Studies in Historical Documents from Nepal and India; https://heiup.uni-heidelberg.de/catalog/view/331/454/80433

event: A western acquisition attributed to Bhutivarman
interpretation: Some historical reconstructions place expansion into parts of Puṇḍravardhana around Bhutivarman’s time. This is the proposed acquisition episode, not a directly dated conquest charter.
limitations: The Badganga and renewed grant evidence do not directly narrate conquest of the whole province; the geography and dating are debated.
ownership_interval_established: No; this is an evidence window, not continuous ownership

event: Gauḍa campaign and proposed North Bengal control
interpretation: Bhaskaravarman’s camp at Karnasuvarna is directly attested. Wider possession of Puṇḍravardhana is a separate historical reconstruction, not a boundary supplied by that camp formula.
limitations: This does not establish the acquisition date, recovery of a precisely defined Ratnapīṭha, or uninterrupted possession.
ownership_interval_established: No; this is an evidence window, not continuous ownership

event: Puṇḍravardhana and Kāmarūpa are described separately
interpretation: The itinerary travels east from Puṇḍravardhana across a large river to Kamarupa. This geographic description must be read alongside, rather than erased by, reconstructions of Bhaskaravarman’s western campaigns.
limitations: Separate descriptions are not by themselves a dated record of defeat or loss by Kamarupa.
ownership_interval_established: No; this is an evidence window, not continuous ownership

date_qualification: Eighth century · identification and date vary
interpretation: The Paśupati inscription’s regional lordship title supplies another western-reach claim. It does not explicitly say that Ratnapīṭha or Puṇḍravardhana was recovered.
limitations: A royal title is not converted into a dated reconquest or an administrative province boundary.
ownership_interval_established: No; this is an evidence window, not continuous ownership

event: A proposed renewed North Bengal connection
interpretation: Historians have used Vanamala’s grant geography to reconstruct authority in Puṇḍravardhana or North Bengal. This proposed reassertion is included in the timeline with the identification dispute visible.
limitations: The place identifications are contested; the record does not explicitly announce recovery of a lost Ratnapīṭha.
ownership_interval_established: No; this is an evidence window, not continuous ownership

event: A victory in Gauḍa and an advance towards the Ganges
interpretation: Gachtal verse 15 reports the defeat of Rajyapala of Gauḍa. It is relevant to western influence, but an explicit recapture of Puṇḍravardhana or Ratnapīṭha is not stated.
limitations: A campaign report cannot establish ownership of the whole province between recorded events.
ownership_interval_established: No; this is an evidence window, not continuous ownership

interpretation: The Belwa plate of Vigrahapala III, regnal year 11, records a grant within Puṇḍravardhana-bhukti. This is direct evidence of Bengal-Pāla administrative activity in the province.
limitations: The year window is for orientation, not a fixed absolute conversion or proof that the whole sacred region changed hands at that date.
ownership_interval_established: No; this is an evidence window, not continuous ownership

actor: Jatavarman of Bengal; Kamarupa ruler uncertain
event: A loss in Puṇḍravardhana attributed to Jatavarman
interpretation: Some historians read the Belava charter’s praise of Jatavarman as evidence that he took a portion of Puṇḍravardhana from Kamarupa. The reported loss is included, without assigning a securely known year or defeated Kamarupa king.
limitations: Sharma questions the political reading of the Kama/rupa wording. It is therefore not shown as a confirmed loss of all Ratnapīṭha.
ownership_interval_established: No; this is an evidence window, not continuous ownership
